pi_agent_loop.Describe the basic agent loop. What make: Call the model, run its tool calls, append the results, repeat. It stops when no more tools are needed (no calls, or every result says terminate) and no steering or follow-up is queued, or right away if the model errors or is aborted.
pi_agent_loop.What is the difference between a steerin: Steering redirects the current run immediately. A follow-up is queued until the agent would otherwise stop.
Steering is checked after each tool batch and before the next model call. Follow-ups are checked only when the run would end.
pi_agent_loop.Why are tool calls in a response that hi: The response was cut off, so the tool call may be incomplete or wrong. Running it could do damage.
pi_agent_loop.Why turn tool exceptions into error resu: A tool error is information the model can act on. A model error means there is no valid response to continue from.
pi_agent_loop.Injecting steering mid-run versus cancel: Injecting keeps the work done so far and reacts quickly but can confuse the context. Restarting is clean but wastes work.
pi_agent_loop.Sequential versus parallel tool executio: Parallel is faster, but you must keep results in call order and avoid tools that conflict, such as edits to the same file.

pi_parallel_tool_batch.Why do agent harnesses run a model's too: Several independent calls such as file reads finish faster together. Result order and hook order must stay deterministic.
pi_parallel_tool_batch.What kinds of tools must never run concu: Tools with side effects on shared state: writes to the same file, shell commands, anything needing sequential semantics.
pi_parallel_tool_batch.Why run every before_tool_call hook befo: Hooks can block or modify calls. If some tools started first, a later hook's decision would come too late.
pi_parallel_tool_batch.How do you return results in call order: Store each result at its call's index, then emit in index order.
pi_parallel_tool_batch.Where is the abort flag checked, and wha: In preparation, after before_tool_call (that call gets "Operation aborted") and after each call (stop preparing; later calls get no message). Then again as each prepared call starts running: it does not execute and gets "Operation aborted".
pi_parallel_tool_batch.Unbounded parallelism versus a bounded p: Unbounded is fastest until rate limits or resource contention hit. A pool bounds them. Sequential is safest and slowest.
pi_parallel_tool_batch.Declaring sequential per tool versus det: Declaring per tool is simple and coarse. Detecting conflicts from arguments is precise but complex and can miss hidden conflicts.

pi_streaming_json.Why would an agent UI parse tool-call ar: To show progress (the file being edited, the command) and start UI work before the call finishes.
pi_streaming_json.Which partial values are safe to show, a: Complete keys and values are safe. Partial numbers (12 of 123), true or false half-written, and dangling escapes must be dropped.
pi_streaming_json.Walk through parsing '{\"path\": \"src/m: The path gives a partial string "src/ma", which is safe to show. For "tr", a literal is unfinished, so drop the key. The parser reports running out inside a value.
pi_streaming_json.What does the repair pass fix, and why a: Raw newlines inside strings and invalid escapes. Models write JSON like prose or code (a regex's \d).
pi_streaming_json.Why try the unrepaired text before the r: If the raw text already parses, repair could only change its meaning. Use repair as a fallback.
pi_streaming_json.Repairing malformed tool arguments versu: Repair is robust but may execute something slightly different from what was intended. Rejecting is safer but costs a retry round trip.
pi_streaming_json.Constrained decoding (grammar-guided JSO: Constrained decoding guarantees valid JSON but needs provider support and can add latency. Repair works anywhere but can guess wrong.

pi_transform_messages.What has to change in a conversation his: Message formats, tool-call id formats, reasoning blocks and provider-specific fields must be converted or dropped.
pi_transform_messages.Why can reasoning blocks from one model: Reasoning may be encrypted or signed for one provider, and another model cannot verify or use it.
pi_transform_messages.Walk through how tool-call ids are norma: Map each old id to a valid new one as you go. The results that follow must use the same mapping, so build it in order.
pi_transform_messages.When is a tool call orphaned, and what d: A call with no result before the next user or assistant message. Insert a synthetic error result. Holding system messages back keeps the call and its result adjacent.
pi_transform_messages.Why skip errored or aborted assistant me: They may contain partial or invalid tool calls. Repairing could invent content. Dropping them is safer.
pi_transform_messages.Converting foreign reasoning to text ver: Converting keeps useful context but costs tokens and may copy another model's style. Dropping loses context.
pi_transform_messages.Repairing malformed histories silently v: Silent repair keeps sessions working but hides bugs. Failing loudly finds them fast but breaks users.

pi_multi_edit.Why do coding agents edit files by strin: Line numbers shift after every edit and full rewrites cost tokens and risk accidental changes. String replacement is anchored to content.
pi_multi_edit.Why must old_text be unique, and what sh: An ambiguous match could edit the wrong place. Report how many matches were found and ask for more context.
Try each old_text exactly. If one is missing but its normalized form matches, turn fuzzy mode on for every edit. Normalization forgives NFKC differences, trailing whitespace, curly quotes, Unicode dashes and special spaces; line endings are unified separately.
pi_multi_edit.Why match all edits against the original: Edits are defined against the file the model saw. Applying from the end keeps earlier offsets valid.
pi_multi_edit.In fuzzy mode, how do you write back onl: Replace only the lines covered by each match in the original text. Writing the normalized file would silently change untouched lines.
pi_multi_edit.String replacement versus unified diffs: Replacement is cheap and precise but needs unique anchors. Diffs are compact but models get the line counts wrong. Rewrites are simple but expensive.
pi_multi_edit.How far would you take fuzzy matching (i: Stop at whitespace and quote normalization. Edit distance risks changing a similar but wrong location.

pi_file_mutation_queue.Why do parallel tool calls in a coding a: Two edits to one file can interleave read-modify-write, so one edit is lost.
pi_file_mutation_queue.Why key the queue by the resolved real p: Different strings (relative paths, symlinks) can refer to the same file. Resolving gives one key per file.
pi_file_mutation_queue.Walk through how each caller waits for t: Chain each caller on the previous one's completion. Delete the key only if no newer caller has queued behind you.
pi_file_mutation_queue.What happens in asyncio if a caller is c: The cancelled waiter must still pass its turn to the next caller, or the chain deadlocks. Use try/finally.
pi_file_mutation_queue.Why must a failing edit still release th: Otherwise the next caller waits forever. Release in finally.
pi_file_mutation_queue.A per-file queue versus one global lock: Per-file allows parallel work on different files. A global lock is simple but serial. Optimistic retries are fast but complex.
pi_file_mutation_queue.Should read operations also go through t: Without it, a read can see a half-applied or older version while a write is pending.

pi_truncate_output.Why must a coding agent truncate tool ou: Huge outputs blow the context and cost. Lines bound the height; bytes bound one very long line.
pi_truncate_output.Why truncate file reads from the head bu: For a file, the start usually matters (headers, definitions). For a command, the end has the errors and results.
pi_truncate_output.Walk through the head loop: what does ea: Each kept line costs its UTF-8 bytes plus 1 for the joining newline, except the first kept line. Stop before a line that would exceed max_bytes (truncated_by bytes); if the loop ends any other way, it is lines.
pi_truncate_output.How do you cut a UTF-8 string to at most: Cut at a byte offset, then move forward past any continuation bytes (10xxxxxx) so you start on a character boundary.
pi_truncate_output.What should the tool tell the model afte: How much was shown and how to get the rest, for example an offset or line number to continue from.
pi_truncate_output.Byte limits versus token limits for tool: Bytes are fast and deterministic but approximate the token cost. Tokens are exact but tokenizer-specific and slower.
pi_truncate_output.Truncating with a note versus spilling t: A note is cheap but loses the rest. Spilling to a file keeps everything searchable but the model must remember to look.

pi_compaction_cut_point.What is context compaction in a coding a: Summarize old history to fit the window. Recent messages carry details the model needs exactly.
pi_compaction_cut_point.Why can the kept range never start at a: A result must follow its call. Starting at a result would keep it without its call.
pi_compaction_cut_point.Walk through choosing the cut: accumulat: Add tokens from the end until the budget is reached, then move to the next valid cut point. A huge trailing result pushes the cut to its call.
pi_compaction_cut_point.What is a split turn, and what extra sum: The cut falls inside a turn, so the kept part lacks the user request that started it. Summarize that request separately.
pi_compaction_cut_point.Why pull adjacent metadata entries into: They describe the kept messages (model change, labels). Separating them loses that context.
pi_compaction_cut_point.Estimated tokens (chars / 4) versus the: Estimates are cheap and available immediately but inaccurate. Reported usage is exact but only known after a call.
pi_compaction_cut_point.Cut-and-summarize compaction versus prun: Compaction loses detail. Pruning loses tool output but keeps structure. Retrieval keeps everything but needs search to find it.
